item.title: England women’s coach Wiegman signs two-year contract extension
item.description: England women’s head coach Sarina Wiegman has signed a two-year contract extension, taking her through until the end of the 2029 women’s European Championship, the Football Association announced Monday. Wiegman has led England to tournament triumphs at both the 2022 and 2025 Euros, as well as a first World Cup final in 2023, since taking charge in September 2021. The 56-year-old Dutchwoman has reached five successive major tournament finals, also winning Euro 2017 with her native Netherlands. “I am so happy to be able to carry on with this squad and cannot think of a better job in football,” Wiegman said Monday. England, beaten by Spain in the 2023 World Cup final in Australia, will face Ukraine over a two-legged play-off in November and December for a place in next year’s tournament in Brazil. “Of course, anyone who knows me will understand that my main concern right now is absolutely the World Cup, and helping this squad realise their potential in the years to come,” Wiegman added. “We have an important job to do to confirm our place in Brazil, and hopefully we can do that and give the country another special summer to remember next year.” Wiegman’s new deal will also encompass the 2027 Nations League, which serves as a qualifying tournament for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. item.description: The southern French city of Marseille has banned all “gatherings and demonstrations” from noon to 8:00 pm (1000-1800 GMT) on Monday, police said, following violence and looting at the weekend during cost-of-living protests. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez is expected to arrive in France’s second-largest city later in the day, after its mayor criticised security arrangements for Saturday’s demonstrations. item.title: Gunmen shoot Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff in Mumbai, three suspects held
item.description: Indian actor Tiger Shroff was shot at in Mumbai on Sunday, police said, adding that three suspects have been detained. Shooters opened fire at the 36-year-old actor as he was leaving a private event in the city’s upscale Juhu area on Sunday evening, according to Police official Mohit Garg. Aside from being India’s financial capital, Mumbai is also the heart of Bollywood, the country’s Hindi-language film industry. “Tiger Shroff is safe and Mumbai police has deployed different teams to investigate further,” Garg told reporters. Two people were injured in the incident, including the actor’s driver, though Shroff did not sustain gunshot wounds, police said. Three suspects have been rounded up in Rajasthan, another Indian state. “Preliminary questioning revealed that two of them have one case each against them, one related to theft and the other under the Arms Act,” police official Tejaswani Gautam told reporters. Police have yet to establish a motive for the shooting. Shroff is known for action films including the “Baaghi” franchise and “War”. item.title: Nigerian newspapers review: Presidency, Makinde in verbal war over N250bn NLNG dividend
item.description: In today’s Nigerian newspapers review programme, Today in the News, Vanguard leads with the Presidency dismissing Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde’s latest claim that the federal government was withholding N250 billion in NLNG dividend windfall for each state in the federation. Another headline features Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, vice-presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), ruling out withdrawal from the 2027 presidential race in favour of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), saying the opposition party offers no better alternative to the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC). Vanguard also reports that revenue collected by Nigeria’s electricity Distribution Companies (DisCos) rose by about 450 per cent in eight years, from N218.16 billion in the first half of 2018 to N1.2 trillion in the corresponding period of 2026, far outpacing growth in electricity supply over the period. Another newspaper, The Guardian, reports that rising rents are outpacing household incomes and forcing tenants into hard trade-offs. The Punch leads with the Federal Government faulting the World Bank’s assessment of Nigeria’s debt position, dismissing concerns that interest payments of N7.7 trillion in the first half of 2026 threaten the country’s debt sustainability. Lastly, The Nation reports that the NDC may be on another collision course with the Obidient Movement after withdrawing recognition of its chapters operating outside Nigeria. item.title: Musk says will give SpaceX share to ‘every kid in America’
item.description: Tech billionaire Elon Musk said on Monday that he would give every child in the United States a share in his SpaceX rocket company. “Next year, I will give one of my SpaceX shares to every kid in America,” Musk, the richest man in the world, said on X. “This will be the first of many,” he said, without providing details about how the scheme would work. There are around 73 million children under the age of 18 in the United States, according to 2024 data from the US Census Bureau. Musk owns 38 percent of SpaceX, according to Forbes. His announcement comes after President Donald Trump promised last month to give every American adult $5,000 if his Republican party retains control of Congress in November’s midterm elections. SpaceX set the record for the largest initial public offering in history, raising $85.7 billion in June. The company’s Starship megarocket reached orbit for the first time in September, a milestone for the rocket central to Musk’s Mars ambitions. item.title: Bauchi: Witchcraft claim sparks violent attack as police arrest 17
item.description: By Christopher Ameh, Bauchi The Bauchi state police command has arrested 17 suspects over an alleged witchcraft accusation that triggered a violent attack on a family in Gobirawa Village, Alkaleri Local Government Area of the state. The suspects allegedly attacked a 60-year-old man and his family after accusing the man’s son of witchcraft following the death of a 20-year-old resident, identified as Halilu Ahmad, on October 16, 2026. The incident occurred around 1am on October 18, when the suspects allegedly invaded the victim’s residence armed with machetes and sticks, inflicting multiple injuries on him and his 30-year-old son. The attackers were also alleged to have damaged two motorcycles belonging to the family. The police said preliminary investigations indicated that the attack was triggered by the suspects’ belief that the victim’s son was responsible for the death through witchcraft. Due to the deteriorating condition of the 60-year-old victim, he was initially taken to General Hospital, Alkaleri, before being referred to Ihsan Hospital, Bauchi, for further treatment. Police spokesman SP Nafiu Habib, who disclosed this in a statement on Monday, said detectives attached to Alkaleri Division arrested the 17 suspects following the incident. He said the commissioner of police, Sani-Omolori Aliyu, had directed the transfer of the case to the State Criminal Investigation Department, SCID, Bauchi, for discreet investigation and the arrest of three other suspects still at large. The police spokesman quoted the commissioner as warning against accusations of witchcraft and other unverified superstitious beliefs that could lead to violence and the unlawful punishment of innocent persons. Aliyu urged residents to report suspicions, grievances and criminal allegations to the police rather than resorting to self-help or jungle justice. He assured the public that the command would pursue justice in the case and would not tolerate actions capable of threatening public peace and security. item.title: UN Agency Slashes Gaza Food Aid Over Funding
item.description: The World Food Programme has said it will end monthly assistance to 500,000 people in Gaza due to a funding shortfall, despite acute needs in the war-battered Palestinian territory. Palestinians arrive at to collect a food ration box provided by the World Food Programme (WFP), at a distribution centre in the village of Al-Zawayda, in the centre of the Gaza Strip on October 27, 2025. Photo by BASHAR TALEB / AFP The World Food Programme said on Monday that its efforts had mitigated the effects during a famine last year in Gaza — a description of the situation disputed by Israel — and warned that conditions had not improved to the point that it can take away aid. “People are not safe. Airstrikes continue on a daily basis. People continue to be displaced,” Shaun Hughes, the WFP country director, told AFP at the agency’s office in east Jerusalem. “Almost everybody remains without a permanent home to live in. And the humanitarian conditions are brutal,” he said. According to the latest assessments, 1.4 million people — or two-thirds of Gaza’s population — are still “acutely food insecure” and need humanitarian assistance to survive, he said. In August last year, the UN’s Integrated Food Security Phase Classification said that Gaza was suffering famine conditions. Israel, which has blockaded the territory and attacked it relentlessly since the unprecedented October 7, 2023 attack on it by Hamas, described the finding as a lie. item.title: African players in Europe: Mbeumo goal eases pressure on Carrick
item.description: Cameroon star Bryan Mbeumo scored his fourth Premier League goal this season for struggling Manchester United in a 1-1 away draw against Leeds United at the weekend. AFP Sport highlights African headline-makers in the major European leagues: ENGLAND BRYAN MBEUMO (Manchester United) Mbeumo netted to ensure under-fire United boss Michael Carrick did not suffer another damaging defeat. Mbeumo put United ahead in the 35th minute against bitter rivals Leeds at Elland Road as he slotted home a Youri Tielemans cross. Leeds hit back to rescue a draw thanks to Dominic Calvert-Lewin’s second-half goal, but avoiding defeat was vital for Carrick after United’s poor start to the season. ALEX IWOBI (Fulham) The Nigeria midfielder’s first goal since March clinched a maiden Premier League win for Cottagers boss Alvaro Arbeloa. Iwobi netted in the 33rd minute of the 1-0 win against Hull at Craven Cottage, taking Sander Berge’s pass and hitting a low strike that squirmed under Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis. item.title: 2027 not a replay of 2023 – Lagos APC tells Peter Obi
item.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos State chapter of the All Progressives Congress (APC) has said presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, risks losing his political capital ahead of the 2027 general elections if he fails to demonstrate ideological consistency and organisational depth. item.title: Wike, Rivers lawmakers meet Fubara
item.description: By Davies Iheamnachor, Port Harcourt The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, has led members of the Rivers State House of Assembly and local government chairmen in the state to a closed-door meeting with the Governor of the state, Siminalayi Fubara. The meeting, whose agenda has not been ascertained, was held at the primate residence of Fubara in Port Harcourt, Sunday evening. The high-profile meeting marked the first time Wike and the lawmakers visited the governor at his residence. The minister had led the delegation, comprising mainly members of the state assembly, led by its speaker, Rt Hon Martin Amaewhule, the candidate of the All Progressives Congress, Kingsley Chinda, and the state’s 23 local government chairmen, and other members of the Rainbow Coalition, to meet with the governor and his supporters. This was coming after an earlier meeting some weeks back in which Wike had also led members of the Rainbow Coalition in the state, including the candidate of the All Progressives Congress in the 2027 general elections, Kingsley Chinda, to meet with Fubara. It was, however, gathered that the Sunday meeting was in continuation of talks between the camps of Wike and Fubara in order to build on the ongoing reconciliation efforts in the state. It was gathered that the meeting was to strengthen efforts to put the political crisis that rocked the state behind and explore ways of accommodating Fubara’s loyalists in the new political setting of 2027. It was learned that at the end of the engagement, Wike and Fubara came out with smiles, likewise the lawmakers, LG Chairmen and other members of the Rainbow Coalition. At the entrance door where they took pictures, the speaker, Amaewhule, and others were captured in a video greeting and shaking hands with the governor, bowing and calling ‘Your Excellency’ even as Fubara acknowledged the greetings with smiles and later rejoined his political godfather, Wike, before all posed for the group photograph. It would be recalled that Fubara and the Amaewhule-led House of Assembly had been entangled in deep war since the political crisis that lasted for over two years following a protracted disagreement between Fubara and his predecessor, Wike. The lawmakers during the heat of the political crisis had on two different occasions attempted to impeach the governor before President Bola Tinubu intervened with the declaration of a state of emergency, suspending the governor and others. Following the disagreement and in spite of the seeming reconciliation, the minister, who is the political leader of the team, ruled out a second tenure stance for Fubara and handed the ticket of the party to Chinda. However, at the verge of the 2027 poll, Wike has resumed moving to bring back all the leaders of his team from the two camps back together. item.title: Trump backs ally Netanyahu ahead of Israel’s tight election
item.description: US President Donald Trump endorsed on Sunday his ally Benjamin Netanyahu before Israel’s close-fought parliamentary election on October 27, providing a boost to the veteran prime minister’s bid to win a new mandate. Netanyahu touted his close relationship with the US president in a video released by his Likud party, saying that together they had “crushed Iran” and adding that re-election would allow him to work with Trump to “elminate the Iranian threat over the next two years, or even sooner”. The endorsement comes less than two weeks before Israel’s first vote since the October 7, 2023 Hamas-led attack, which opposition politicians have accused Netanyahu of bearing personal responsibility for after allegedly ignoring warnings. Trump and Netanyahu, who polls show is in a tight election race, have worked closely together on Israel’s multi-front wars after the Hamas-led attack, including bombarding Iran, and the endorsement could be a boon to his re-election campaign. “Bibi Netanyahu has been Strong, Brave, and Brilliant in the face of tremendous opposition, including that coming from even Israel, itself,” Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform, using a common nickname for the Israeli leader. “This is the kind of Partner that the United States of America is demanding of Israel, a Country for which it has done so much. Please let this Letter serve to represent my Complete and Total Endorsement of Bibi Netanyahu in his upcoming Race for Re-Election as Prime Minister of Israel.” The election is seen as a referendum on Netanyahu, who quickly thanked the US leader for his support on Sunday. “Thank you, President Trump, for your tremendous support and for our work together. item.title: 2027: Vote for candidate who’ll make your money buy more — Alaje advises Nigerians
item.description: Senior economist at SPM Professionals, Paul Alaje, has urged Nigerians to assess presidential candidates in the 2027 general election based on their ability to improve purchasing power, reduce living costs and make essential services more affordable. Alaje said voters should prioritise candidates whose economic policies would enable Nigerians to buy more with their earnings, rather than be swayed by promises of higher wages without corresponding improvements in real income. He made the remarks on Channels Television’s Sunday Politics while discussing the economic policies Nigerians should consider when evaluating candidates ahead of the 2027 presidential election. “Any candidate who is telling you that the money in your pocket will buy more, will improve more, and will afford your rent — that is the candidate you should vote for,” he said. The economist said an increase in nominal earnings would not necessarily translate into better living conditions if prices continued to rise faster than incomes. Explaining the concept of purchasing power, Alaje said Nigerians should consider what their earnings could buy and whether proposed economic policies would improve their ability to meet household needs. “You can earn more in naira terms. Like labour wants more money, you can. But will it buy more in real terms?” he asked. He said voters should examine candidates’ plans for making education more affordable, improving access to healthcare and addressing other pressures on household budgets. According to him, the central question should be which candidate can improve the real value of Nigerians’ earnings and make essential services accessible to more people. Alaje also warned that economic policies that fail to prioritise productivity could undermine the country’s economic performance. “Anybody who is not discussing productivity is going to run the economy down,” he said. He argued that productivity and other economic fundamentals must support reforms if they are to deliver sustainable improvements in living standards. 2027: Alaje urges Tinubu to address electricity The economist also called on President Bola Tinubu to take urgent steps to address Nigeria’s electricity challenges, describing power supply as a critical factor in improving economic performance. “You need to do something urgent and critical about electricity,” he told the President. Alaje said countries that had successfully implemented reforms similar to Nigeria’s had underlying economic fundamentals that helped them achieve results. “Major economies that adopted the kind of reforms we are adopting and have results, they have fundamentals working for them,” he said. item.title: PANDEF declares seven days of mourning for Dele Cole
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Pan Niger Delta Forum (PANDEF), the apex socio-political body of the South-South geopolitical zone, has declared seven days of mourning in honour of its leader and elder statesman, Patrick Dele Cole, who died in London at the age of 86. Cole, popularly known as Chief PDC, died weeks after celebrating his 86th birthday, leaving behind a legacy of service in journalism, education, diplomacy, public administration and politics. In a statement signed by PANDEF National Chairman, Ambassador Godknows Igali, on behalf of the organisation’s Board of Trustees (BoT) and National Executive Committee (NEC), the forum described Cole’s death as a painful and irreplaceable loss. Igali said Cole played significant roles in the socio-cultural and political development of the Niger Delta, particularly in the formation and growth of PANDEF. The late Cole served as Editor-in-Chief of the Daily Times of Nigeria, one of the country’s leading national newspapers, and later as presidential adviser on foreign affairs. He also served as Nigeria’s ambassador to Brazil. According to Igali, Cole brought considerable intellectual depth and experience to various socio-cultural and socio-political organisations in the Niger Delta. PANDEF directed all its chapters in Nigeria and the diaspora to suspend official social activities for seven days, beginning October 18, 2026. It also directed that Cole’s photograph be displayed on its media platforms throughout the mourning period. Igali said Cole played a significant role in the region’s struggle for true federalism and resource control, noting that his commitment to the aspirations of the Niger Delta people remained firm even while he served as a special adviser in the administration of former President Olusegun Obasanjo. He added that Cole’s political choices were guided by his commitment to the interests and legitimate aspirations of the Niger Delta people. Cole’s political career included a presidential bid under the Social Democratic Party (SDP) and membership of the Board of Trustees of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), PANDEF said. The forum also acknowledged his contributions as a Christian leader and advocate of Nigeria’s cultural heritage, particularly the traditions and identities of the South-South region. Expressing condolences over his death, PANDEF extended its sympathies to his son, Rt. Hon. Tonye Cole, other members of the Cole family, the people of Abonnema in the Kalabari Kingdom, the Ijaw nation, the Rivers State Government and the people of Rivers State, as well as Nigerians across the country. The organisation urged the bereaved family and the wider Niger Delta community to draw comfort from the distinguished life and enduring contributions of the late elder statesman. PANDEF prayed for the peaceful repose of Cole’s soul. The post PANDEF declares seven days of mourning for Dele Cole appeared first on Vanguard News .

Describing him as a person who never flaunted his privileged family background, Abari said Kashim was well brought up, good-natured and friendly to people regardless of their social standing. “He was a personification of humility, never carrying any airs around him about the kind of family he came from,” he said. Abari added that although Kashim came from a political family and held his own political views, he never allowed political differences to damage his relationships with others. The former NOA director-general said the suddenness of the death was a reminder of the uncertainty of human life. “If I recall the moments we had together, I recall the banters, everything. They later observed the Asr prayer at the mosque before Kashim dropped him at his residence at about 4:30pm. Yusuf said he received a call from Kashim’s son about half an hour later, informing him that the family had been told that his father’s car was involved in an accident in Asokoro and that the occupant had been taken to Asokoro General Hospital. Kashim was also known by the traditional title of Shettima of Borno, a title associated with his family’s longstanding place in the traditional and political history of the region. Yusuf said the title had a historical connection to his father, Sir Kashim Ibrahim, who was conferred with the title of Shettima of Borno in 1935 and later became Waziri of Borno in 1956. Although his father occupied a prominent position in the country’s political history, Abari said Kashim remained approachable and maintained friendships with people of different backgrounds and political persuasions. item.title: Nigeria joins league of nations in global measurement pact
item.description: By Adaobi Abimbola Nigeria has joined the league of nations with globally recognised measurement standards following the signing of the Mutual Recognition Arrangement of the International Committee for Weights and Measures, CIPM MRA, in France. The agreement was signed by the Director-General of the Standards Organisation of Nigeria, SON, Dr Ifeanyi Chukwunonso Okeke, at the 28th General Conference on Weights and Measures CGPM. The signing coincided with the DG’s third anniversary in office. According to a statement made by SON’s Director of Corporate Affairs, Mrs. Ethan Talatu, Nigeria’s admission as an Associate State of the International Bureau of Weights and Measures, BIPM, took effect on June 4, 2026. The CIPM MRA is the framework through which national metrology institutes prove that their measurement standards are equivalent and earn global recognition for their calibration and measurement certificates. Okeke said that the arrangement would bring international recognition of Nigeria’s measurement capabilities, global acceptance of its calibration certificates and easier trade across borders. He added that it would reduce dependence on foreign metrology services, strengthen SON’s technical authority and open doors to scientific collaboration and capacity building. Nigeria now joins Egypt, Kenya, Morocco, South Africa and Tunisia as the only African countries with full BIPM membership. For manufacturers and small businesses, products can be tested locally and trusted abroad without the cost of foreign laboratories. item.title: FG targets $7.1bn sugar investments, 110,000 jobs in 10 years
item.description: The Federal Government is targeting $7.1 billion in investments in the sugar industry over 10 years to boost domestic production above two million metric tonnes annually, create 110,000 jobs and save $2.1 billion in foreign exchange annually. The programme, coordinated by the National Sugar Development Council (NSDC), is aimed at reducing Nigeria’s dependence on imported raw sugar through increased sugarcane cultivation, processing capacity and private-sector investment. Executive Secretary of NSDC, Kamar Bakrin, disclosed the plan in Abuja, saying the initiative would strengthen local production and supporting agricultural infrastructure. Under the programme, the council is proposing 10 integrated sugar estates across Niger, Kwara, Oyo, Kaduna, Jigawa, Bauchi, Nasarawa and Adamawa states. The estates are expected to cover 143,478 hectares, with a combined milling capacity of 55,500 metric tonnes of sugarcane daily. According to NSDC, the proposed estates could produce 835,000 metric tonnes of sugar annually, while existing operators are expected to contribute another 1.22 million tonnes through increased output. The projects are also expected to support ethanol production and electricity generation, creating additional opportunities for agro-processing and value addition. To finance the programme, the council is seeking $5 billion in long-term debt and $2.1 billion in equity contributions from investors. Funding is expected to involve export credit agencies, development finance institutions and local financial organisations. NSDC also disclosed a $1 billion agreement with Chinese engineering company Sinomach, although the associated financing arrangements are yet to be completed. It is collaborating with the Bank of Industry on a proposed N10 billion Sugar Projects Acceleration Fund to support feasibility studies and prepare projects for investment. item.title: Manufacturing index plunges 10% as cement sector contracts – NESG
item.description: By Yinka Kolawole Nigeria’s manufacturing business activity plunged by about 10 per cent in September 2026, as a contraction in the cement subsector and weakening performance across several industries dragged down the sector’s business index, the Nigerian Economic Summit Group (NESG) has said. The group’s Business Confidence Monitor (BCM) showed that the manufacturing Current Business Performance Index (CBPI) fell to 108.4 points in September from 120.4 points in August, amid persistent cost pressures, tight credit conditions and operational challenges. Despite the manufacturing setback, overall business activity maintained its expansionary momentum, with the composite CBPI rising to 117.8 points from 112.7 points in August and 107.9 points in September 2025. According to the NESG, expansion was recorded across all major sectors, with trade delivering the strongest performance. The sector’s index rose sharply to 128.5 points from 112.0 points in August. The manufacturing slowdown reflected mixed performances among the sector’s largest subsectors. Food, Beverage and Tobacco remained in expansion territory but recorded slower activity, while Textile, Apparel and Footwear performed more strongly than in the preceding month. Cement, however, moved into contraction. Business activity also contracted in Chemical and Pharmaceutical Products, Plastic and Rubber Products, Wood and Wood Products, Non-Metallic Products, Basic Metal, Iron and Steel, and Motor Vehicles and Assembly. Pulp, Paper and Paper Products remained in expansion, although its index was unchanged, while Electrical and Electronics recorded stronger activity. Other manufacturing held around the 100-point threshold separating expansion from contraction. The report identified energy shortages, inadequate raw-material supplies, high rental costs, tight credit conditions and infrastructure deficiencies as major constraints facing manufacturers. These challenges increased operating costs and discouraged fresh investment. In agriculture, the CBPI rose to 117.7 points in September from 110.5 points in August and 107.3 points a year earlier. Crop production and agro-allied activities recorded stronger expansion, while livestock activity slowed. Forestry and fishing moved into contraction. The sector nevertheless faced inadequate financing, power outages, insecurity and infrastructure bottlenecks. Meanwhile, services activity slowed, with its index declining to 107.7 points from 112.4 points in August, although it remained in expansion territory. The NESG’s findings indicate that stronger trade and agricultural activity supported the broader economy, even as mounting cost pressures and operational constraints continued to undermine manufacturing performance. item.title: Manufacturers seek 30% green tax credit to cut energy cost
item.description: By Yinka Kolawole Manufacturers have called on the Federal Government to introduce a 30 per cent Green Investment Tax Credit for companies investing in renewable energy and hybrid power solutions, as rising energy costs continue to undermine industrial productivity and push up production costs. Director General of the Manufacturers Association of Nigeria (MAN), Segun Ajayi-Kadir, in the 2025 Annual Report of the association, said the proposed incentive would encourage manufacturers to transition to off-grid renewable energy and hybrid captive power systems, including solar and liquefied natural gas (LNG), to reduce their dependence on expensive and unstable energy sources. The proposal comes as manufacturers’ annual expenditure on alternative energy rose by 20.72 per cent to N1.34 trillion in 2025, from N1.11 trillion in 2024, reflecting the growing burden of providing electricity for factory operations. Ajayi-Kadir said the government needed to adopt targeted fiscal and energy-sector reforms to lower operating costs, improve industrial competitiveness and ease the inflationary pressures associated with expensive production. item.title: Gas marketers push for safer, smarter, more compliant LPG operations
item.description: By Sebastine Obasi The Nigerian Association of Liquefied Petroleum Gas Marketers (NALPGAM) has called on industry operators to prioritise safety, regulatory compliance and digitalisation to drive sustainable growth in Nigeria’s liquid petroleum gas (LPG) sector. The call was made at its 2026 webinar last week with the theme; “Downstream LPG Operational Excellence and Compliance,” which brought together industry operators, regulators and other stakeholders to address safety risks, market volatility, operational losses and regulatory requirements. In his opening address, Mr. Edu Inyang, National President, NALPGAM, stated: “The future of Nigeria’s LPG industry cannot be achieved by increasing volumes alone. We must grow safely, responsibly, efficiently and sustainably. Safety is not an occasional campaign; it must become a continuous industry culture.” A key outcome was the adoption of the aspiration for a “NALPGAM Standard of Operational Excellence,” built on four principles: safe and well-maintained facilities, competent and trained operators, compliant processes, and customer protection. Participants urged operators to embed safety in daily operations, strengthen preventive maintenance, comply with licensing and incident-reporting requirements, and eliminate unsafe practices, including unauthorised propane blending and illegal decanting. “Compliance is not merely a regulatory burden; it is a business advantage. Well-managed LPG operations reduce accidents, improve efficiency, protect investments and strengthen public confidence in our industry,” Inyang said. The webinar also highlighted digital technologies including smart filling systems, automated tank gauges, load cells, flow meters and vehicle tracking as practical tools to reduce product losses, improve accountability and strengthen operational efficiency. item.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, October 19, 2026
item.description: The dollar-to-naira exchange rate opened the new trading week on Monday, October 19, 2026, with the official Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM) rate around ₦1,333.54 per dollar, according to available exchange-rate data. The parallel market rate remains higher, with recent reports indicating that Bureau De Change operators sell the dollar at rates that vary by location and dealer. According to the latest available figures for Monday, October 19, the exchange rates are as follows: Official NFEM rate: approximately ₦1,333.54 per dollar. Parallel market buying rate: approximately ₦1,375 per dollar. Parallel market selling rate: approximately ₦1,390 per dollar. The parallel market figures are indicative quotes and may vary depending on the dealer, location and transaction size. Naira outlook The naira ended the previous trading week relatively stable in the official market, with the exchange rate closing at around ₦1,332.26 per dollar on Friday, October 16. In the parallel market, the dollar sold for about ₦1,370, according to market reports. The difference between the official rate of ₦1,333.54 and the parallel market selling rate of ₦1,390 is approximately ₦56.46 per dollar. Forex rates may change during the day as demand and supply conditions shift. Individuals and businesses are advised to confirm prevailing rates with their banks or licensed foreign exchange dealers before conducting transactions.
